record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Can microscopic models for manganites realize either a homogeneous spin-canted ground state at zero magnetic field or a phase diagram in which a charge-ordered antiferromagnetic state appears at intermediate temperatures while a ferromagnetic metallic state becomes stable at lower temperature?

evidence.quote: Are there models with spin canted homogeneous ground states? ... Can a model develop a charge-ordered AF phase at intermediate temperatures while having a ferromagnetic metallic phase at low temperatures?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider microscopic lattice models for doped manganites (mixed-valence perovskites of the form R_{1-x}A_x MnO_3, with R a rare earth and A a divalent cation), built from itinerant e_g electrons on Mn sites hopping between nearest neighbors, Hund-coupled to localized t_{2g} core spins (treated either classically or as S=3/2 quantum spins), together with on-site and nearest-neighbor Coulomb repulsion, Jahn-Teller and breathing-mode electron-phonon couplings to the e_g orbitals, and a direct antiferromagnetic superexchange J_AF between neighboring t_{2g} spins. Generic Hamiltonians of this type include the one- and two-orbital double-exchange models with Jahn-Teller phonons and Coulomb interactions on two- or three-dimensional cubic lattices.

Address the following two model-building questions:

(a) Does there exist a choice of such a microscopic Hamiltonian and a region of its parameter space (including doping x) for which the exact ground state at zero external magnetic field is a spatially homogeneous spin-canted state, i.e., a state with uniform sublattice magnetizations m_A and m_B on the two sublattices of a bipartite lattice making a fixed angle 0 < θ < π with each other, with no phase separation into ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic regions?

(b) Does there exist a choice of such a microscopic Hamiltonian and a region of its parameter space whose finite-temperature phase diagram exhibits, upon cooling at fixed doping and zero magnetic field, a transition from a paramagnetic phase into a charge-ordered antiferromagnetic insulating phase at an intermediate temperature T_CO, followed by a further transition at a lower temperature T_FM < T_CO into a ferromagnetic metallic phase (so that the ferromagnetic metallic phase is the true low-temperature equilibrium phase, with the charge-ordered antiferromagnetic phase appearing only at intermediate temperatures)?
artifact.category_tag: Strongly correlated electron models for manganites
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on manganite model phase diagrams reveal extensive literature on competing ferromagnetic metallic, charge-ordered antiferromagnetic, and canted antiferromagnetic phases, with phase separation widely accepted instead of homogeneous canting in realistic parameter regimes. No definitive theoretical construction of a microscopic manganite model with a homogeneous spin-canted ground state at zero field is established, and reentrant FM-metallic-below-CO-AF phase diagrams in microscopic models do not appear to be conclusively demonstrated. The status of both model-building questions therefore remains unclear from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Mixed-valence manganites (Coey, Viret, von Molnár)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews competing FM metallic, CO-AF and canted phases in manganites, treating canting both as homogeneous order and as a signature of phase separation.
status_evidence.claim: Homogeneous canted states are debated versus phase-separated descriptions in manganite models.

status_evidence.title: Visualization of a ferromagnetic metallic edge state in manganite strips
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses coexistence and competition of FM metallic and CO-AF insulating phases in manganites.
status_evidence.claim: FM-metallic and CO-AF phases are competing ground states whose relative stability is parameter-dependent.
